issues.description: `lemma_va_range_get_guard_level` exports the guard-level bound used for path indexing and loop invariants while its entire proof body is `admit()`.
issues.rationale: For every well-formed virtual-address range, callers may assume `1 <= va_range_get_guard_level(va) <= 4`, but the selected snapshot provides no checked derivation. `lock_range` invokes the lemma before indexing its path and maintaining level bounds. Repair 9000178e adds a decreasing recursive lemma over levels 1 through 4 and uses it to discharge exactly this guarantee.
issues.source_evidence: after/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/cursor.rs:165-172 declares the callable bound and closes it with `admit()`. The same selected file calls it in `lock_range` at lines 261-262. Repair 9000178ee84b7a61db2212916a14b48cbf4fd308 adds `lemma_va_range_get_guard_level_rec` and replaces the admit with a checked call.
issues.verification: Compatible historical Verus reports a passing problem target because `admit()` is trusted. Fixed-source primary and independent reviews confirm the unchecked guard-level theorem and that repair 9000178e replaces only this admit with a recursive proof.

issues.description: `lemma_va_range_get_tree_path` exports valid NodeIds and the exact guard-path length while its entire proof body is `admit()`.
issues.rationale: `lock_range` consumes the theorem immediately after the guard-level lemma and may rely on every generated path node being valid and on `path.len() == 5 - guard_level`. Those are separate structural guarantees not established by the guard-level numeric bound. Repair 623d3a17 proves trace length and trace validity recursively and derives both exported path facts.
issues.source_evidence: after/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/cursor.rs:183-195 declares both guarantees and closes them with `admit()`. Repair 623d3a17a87382ce4b7e8dfb9b95600727f7fe86 adds trace-length/validity lemmas and a checked proof of each path element and the exact length.
issues.verification: Compatible historical Verus accepts the selected snapshot because the body is trusted. Source and independent reviews confirm this distinct path-validity/length obligation and its complete removal by repair 623d3a17.

issues.description: `NodeHelper::lemma_is_child_level_relation` exports the one-level parent/child relationship while its entire proof body is `admit()`.
issues.rationale: Cursor descent can treat every valid child as exactly one paging level below its parent without deriving that fact from `is_child`. This is a general NodeHelper relation, distinct from the virtual-address range and trace theorems. Repair 5160ce04 derives subtree membership and applies established level/depth relations for both nodes.
issues.source_evidence: after/lock-protocol/src/spec/utils.rs:1648-1657 states `nid_to_level(pa) == nid_to_level(ch) + 1` and ends in `admit()`. The selected cursor calls the theorem during descent at line 369. Repair 5160ce043de84bf2edb9b96d94357c1774c20316 replaces the admit with three checked helper calls.
issues.verification: The selected snapshot verifies only because the parent/child theorem is trusted. Fixed Git comparison and independent review confirm that repair 5160ce04 proves this general level relation without changing its contract.

issues.description: `lemma_va_level_to_nid_inc` exports the correspondence between virtual-address traces and the next child NodeId while its entire proof body is `admit()`.
issues.rationale: A cursor descent step may identify `get_child(nid, idx)` with the NodeId for the next lower virtual-address level without a checked connection between consecutive traces, the extracted offset, and the trace/NodeId bijection. Repair 86257079 proves those trace and offset facts and then derives the exact child equality.
issues.source_evidence: after/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/common.rs:127-139 declares the child-NodeId equality and ends in `admit()`. The selected cursor invokes it at lines 363-368. Repair 86257079bec7c99f2c803970a9d4676f9d182b23 replaces the admit with the consecutive-trace, bit-shift/offset, valid-trace, and bijection proof and relocates shared trace helpers without changing them.
issues.verification: The problem and final snapshots pass with compatible historical Verus because the problem admit is trusted. Source comparison and independent review confirm the distinct trace-to-child theorem and the checked final repair.
